commit_message:
avformat/mov: add option max_stts_delta

Very high stts sample deltas may occasionally be intended but usually
they are written in error or used to store a negative value for dts correction
when treated as signed 32-bit integers.

This option lets the user set an upper limit, beyond which the delta is clamped to 1.
Values greater than the limit if negative when cast to int32 are used to adjust onward dts.

Unit is the track time scale. Default is UINT_MAX - 48000*10 which
allows upto a 10 second dts correction for 48 kHz audio streams while
accommodating 99.9% of uint32 range.

Signed-off-by: Gyan Doshi <ffmpeg@gyani.pro>
Reviewed-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

 Fixed key used for handling Audible AAX/AAX+ files. It has been pre-set so should not be necessary to

 @item decryption_key
 16-byte key, in hex, to decrypt files encrypted using ISO Common Encryption (CENC/AES-128 CTR; ISO/IEC 23001-7).
+
+@item max_stts_delta
+Very high sample deltas written in a trak's stts box may occasionally be intended but usually they are written in
+error or used to store a negative value for dts correction when treated as signed 32-bit integers. This option lets
+the user set an upper limit, beyond which the delta is clamped to 1. Values greater than the limit if negative when

+
+Unit is the track time scale. Range is 0 to UINT_MAX. Default is @code{UINT_MAX - 48000*10} which allows upto
+a 10 second dts correction for 48 kHz audio streams while accommodating 99.9% of @code{uint32} range.
 @end table
 
 @subsection Audible AAX
 
 Audible AAX files are encrypted M4B files, and they can be decrypted by specifying a 4 byte activation secret.
 @example
 ffmpeg -activation_bytes 1CEB00DA -i test.aax -vn -c:a copy output.mp4
 @end example

fix_commit_message:
avformat/mov: fix overflow in drift timestamp calculation

Fixes: signed integer overflow: 7803923888585309955 - -3407677434275325337 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t' (aka 'long')
Fixes: 377736723/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-media_pipeline_integration_fuzzer-5052449500889088

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 02958ab7156b on top of intro 9cfc7a244052 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): libavformat/mov.c's mov_read_stts() parses the 'stts' (sample-to-time / time-to-sample) box in MOV/MP4 files, tracking two int64_t accumulators, current_dts and corrected_dts, derived from file-supplied 32-bit sample_count and sample_duration values (including a max_stts_delta correction path that reinterprets large unsigned durations as signed int32 deltas). When these two accumulators diverge to very large values of opposite sign after processing many crafted stts entries, the plain signed subtraction 'current_dts - corrected_dts' used to compute a drift correction can overflow int64_t, which is undefined behavior in C. OSS-Fuzz's UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer flagged this while fuzzing the media pipeline integration fuzzer. Root cause: The max_stts_delta feature (added in commit 9cfc7a2440) introduced accumulation of two independently-growing int64_t DTS trackers (current_dts, corrected_dts) driven directly by untrusted 32-bit file fields, and then performed unchecked signed subtraction between them to derive a 'drift' correction value without validating that the operands stay within a range where the subtraction cannot overflow int64_t.
